newsitem.title: USA: Armey says U.S. Republicans committed to tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Armey says U.S. Republicans committed to tax cuts.

text.p: House Majority Leader Dick Armey he was committed to working out a balanced budget deal that included "substantial tax cuts" but held out the possibility Republicans would craft their own plan if they could not reach agreement with the White House.
Speaking to reporters, the Texas Republican said lawmakers should give President Clinton "every bit of encouragement we can" to work out a budget.
Asked if Republicans would have to write their own budget bill, he said "we'll probably come to that. We haven't come to that yet."
Armey said talks set for today between congressional budget leaders and the White House were important "to see if we can start pinning things down a little better."
"We want a balanced budget that realistically deals with the threat Medicare is facing. ... We clearly need to have a substantial tax reduction in the end product," Armey said.

Asked why Republicans had not developed their own budget yet, he said lawmakers could either "negotiate at the beginning of a Congress or you can negotiate at the end of a Congress. I would much rather like to negotiate with the president at the beginning of the process."
